title: An ER diagram for a clinic
instructions:
## Entities, attributes and crow's feet

A clinic keeps **Patients** (id, name, date of birth), **Doctors** (id, name, specialty) and **Appointments** (id, date, notes). A patient has many appointments; each appointment is with exactly one doctor and one patient; a doctor has many appointments. Each appointment may produce one **Prescription** (id, drug, dosage).

## Do this

Write the ER diagram: four entities with attributes and a primary key each (mark it `PK`), and the relationships with crow's-foot cardinalities and a verb: `PATIENT ||--o{ APPOINTMENT : attends`.
hints: ||--o{ reads "exactly one to zero or more".
APPOINTMENT ||--o| PRESCRIPTION : produces (zero or one prescription).

checks.label: Appointment to at most one prescription
Every entity has attributes and a primary key; every relationship has a verb

realityNote: This diagram becomes CREATE TABLE statements almost mechanically: each "many" side gets a foreign key to the "one" side. The database labs in this course take the same clinic into SQL.
